entities.summary:
Guiguzi (鬼谷子), a foundational collection of ancient Chinese texts, was compiled between 399 BCE and 25 BCE during the Warring States period and the Han dynasty.

This influential work of rhetoric, comprising approximately 6,000 to 7,000 Chinese characters, was initially associated with the School of Diplomacy but was later integrated into the Daoist canon.

Guiguzi's significance extends beyond its historical context, as it has shaped the development of Chinese thought and intellectual traditions.

The Guiguzi's impact can be seen in its continued relevance in modern Chinese philosophy and its influence on the work of prominent thinkers such as Zhuangzi.

As a testament to its enduring importance, the Guiguzi has been translated into multiple languages and continues to be studied by scholars and philosophers worldwide.

The Guiguzi's legacy is also reflected in its incorporation into the curricula of Chinese universities and its use as a primary source in academic research.

In conclusion, the Guiguzi represents a pivotal moment in the evolution of Chinese intellectual history, and its continued relevance underscores its significance as a foundational text in Chinese philosophy.
